description: We are building an interactive, high-impact surface change visualization platform powered by data from the joint NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission.
summary:
Earth Signal is an interactive platform prototype that makes NASA–ISRO NISAR radar observations easier to discover, explore and understand. Users can start with a geographic location or choose an Earth-system topic, including water and wetlands, ground movement, forests and vegetation, agriculture, and ice and glaciers.

The platform connects location-based discovery with NISAR observation metadata, interactive geographic visualization, acquisition timelines and data-readiness checks. It helps users identify available satellite observations, understand their coverage and maturity, and determine which types of surface-change investigations are possible. For supported analyses, users can compare observations over time, inspect measured changes and examine the underlying evidence and limitations.

Earth Signal aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite radar data and accessible Earth observation insights, helping researchers, educators and environmental organizations explore how our planet is changing.
details:
EARTH SIGNAL — Discover. Understand. Monitor.

Overview

Earth Signal is an interactive, map-first platform for discovering and inspecting satellite radar observations from the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission.

The project addresses a practical barrier in Earth observation: although SAR data can reveal changes across land, vegetation, water and ice, finding relevant observations and understanding their technical characteristics is not straightforward for users outside specialist remote-sensing workflows.

Earth Signal brings geographic discovery, observation metadata and temporal context into one interface.

What the Platform Does

The application is organized around a location-first exploration workflow. Users can begin with a geographic area or coordinates, explore available observations and inspect the underlying data records.

Its principal capabilities include:

  • Geographic exploration: An interactive CesiumJS 3D globe provides the primary interface for navigating observation areas and spatial footprints.
  • NISAR data discovery: The application queries the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) search service to retrieve relevant observation records.
  • Observation catalogue: Users can filter and explore records by acquisition date and product type.
  • Temporal exploration: An acquisition timeline organizes available observations and helps users identify candidate repeat-pass records.
  • Observation inspection: Granule details expose available metadata, browse imagery and source assets.
  • Soil-moisture exploration: The prototype includes a spatial visualization of a NISAR Level-3 SME2 soil-moisture sample.
  • Saved locations: Watchpoint functionality provides a way to retain geographic areas for later inspection.

How It Works

The application connects the ASF observation catalogue to a geographic interface.

A user searches for an area or selects coordinates. The backend retrieves matching NISAR records and makes their spatial and temporal metadata available to the frontend. CesiumJS presents the geographic context, while catalogue and inspection views expose the associated granule information and available assets.

Server-side API functions handle ASF search requests and Earthdata asset resolution. Supabase provides the PostgreSQL/PostGIS data layer and storage infrastructure used by the application.

The interface is designed to preserve the connection between an observation and its source record, rather than presenting satellite imagery without provenance.

Scientific Approach and Limitations

NISAR products serve different scientific purposes. Product type, processing level, acquisition geometry, data maturity and quality information all affect what can be investigated responsibly.

Earth Signal therefore focuses on making observations and their technical context easier to discover and inspect.

The current prototype is primarily a discovery and inspection tool. Pair selection and browse-image comparisons are exploratory; they should not be interpreted as validated InSAR displacement estimates or calibrated quantitative change detection. The SME2 visualization is an exploratory sample, not a global operational soil-moisture service.

The project does not present unvalidated displacement, glacier velocity, biomass-loss or inundation measurements as scientific results.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Earth Signal reduces the initial complexity of working with satellite radar data by connecting geographic locations to the observations available for them.

It is intended to help students, researchers, educators and environmental practitioners identify relevant NISAR observations, understand their coverage and inspect the source data before deciding whether a deeper scientific analysis is appropriate.

The broader goal is to make Earth-observation data more accessible while preserving the scientific context required to interpret it correctly.

Technology and Implementation

The application uses:

  • React 18 and Vite for the web application.
  • CesiumJS for 3D geospatial visualization.
  • JavaScript and Vercel serverless functions for application logic and API integration.
  • NASA ASF Search services for NISAR observation discovery.
  • NASA Earthdata services for protected data-asset access.
  • Supabase, PostgreSQL and PostGIS for metadata, spatial records and storage.

Design and Engineering Considerations

The project prioritizes location-first navigation, clear observation metadata, spatial context and temporal organization. The interface separates catalogue discovery from inspection of individual data products.

It also considers the differences between NISAR product types and their processing maturity. This is important because observations from different product levels or processing versions cannot automatically be treated as interchangeable evidence.

Responsible Use of Data and Super Intelligence

NASA and partner-agency resources are identified in the project references. Third-party software and source materials are acknowledged.

Super Intelligence tools were used during ideation, research, coding assistance, debugging and project documentation. Any AI-generated visual assets included in the submitted deliverables are identified as AI-generated concept material and are not represented as actual NISAR observations.

Scientific observations and measurements are sourced from the underlying satellite data; AI-generated content is not used as a substitute for scientific evidence.
